producedBy: Captain, from a read-only audit lane's diff reading, with every decisive claim re-measured independently before it was recorded here
question: For each first-cohort candidate, does any change made after the decision owner's completed-output approval fall in the class that requires a NEW decision, or is it all in the class the existing approval already covers?
howTheTestWorks: The decision record carries its own two lists. correctionsNotRequiringANewLegalDecision covers renderer wiring, field mapping, PDF flattening, active-content removal, text fitting, caption correction, a source hash refresh for the same form and revision, visual fixes, storage integration, route-to-family wiring, packet-builder wiring and deterministic fixture corrections. requiresANewDecisionOwnerDecision covers changing the remedy, eligibility logic, a mandatory filing, venue, the required recipient or service party, replacing a mandatory official form with a custom pleading, and adding substantive legal language not already present in the approved design. A change is read against those lists and nothing else.
whyAnUnchangedPacketProofIsNotEnough: For the original three candidates, packetProofSha256 and legalDesignMemoSha256 are unchanged since the approval, and that is necessary rather than sufficient. Those packet proofs attest implementation outputs under src/lib/rcap/packets/jurisdictions/ and scripts/verify-rcap-*-custom-pleading.mjs, and none of those paths exists in this checkout — the shipping artifacts come from the census-v1 generator instead. The proofs are unchanged because nothing touched them, not because they describe what now ships. So coverage was decided by reading the rendered output against the unchanged legal design memo, not by trusting the proof hash.
method: For the original three candidates, each legal design memo was flattened into a string corpus, every memo fragment of thirty characters or more was removed from the normalised text of the rendered canonical fixture and the participant instructions, and the residue of sixty characters or more was read by hand. For the 2026-09-04 Georgia expansion, the exact post-approval path history, approved memo and manifest, later route contract, instructions, field map, build findings and both four-page fixture PDFs were read in full; hashes and page counts were re-measured and every PDF page was visually inspected. For the six-family 2026-09-04 expansion at 072f97bf1c92b1f6de0ccca565734da1cc285456, the selected September approval and its two controlling lists, every family-path and builder commit after approval, both fixture texts and their canonical-to-boundary diffs, current source receipts, exact legal-design and packet-set objects, exact obligation-census and compiled-pathway objects, applicable route-contract objects, participant instructions, component manifests, fee, waiver, service, notice, hearing and stop language, current independent verdicts and current raster pins were read; every stated hash and page count was independently recomputed from the committed bytes. COVERED is recorded only when that evidence places every post-approval delta on the owner's existing-approval list.
